concerns.location: plan.md:Section 2 – Network Construction / Synthetic Control (MDS coordinates)
concerns.text: The plan derives node Euclidean coordinates via Classical MDS on the all‑pairs shortest‑path distance matrix of the *same* Barabási‑Albert graph that is later used for SIR transmission. Consequently, the distance‑based transmission probability βᵢⱼ = β₀·e^{‑λ·dᵢⱼ} is a deterministic function of the underlying topology. The validation compares this ‘spatial’ model against a null that randomises those MDS‑derived coordinates. Because both the predictor (distance) and the outcome (epidemic spread) are rooted in the same topology, the analysis cannot cleanly isolate an *independent* geographic effect; it risks a circular/tautological validation where any observed difference may simply reflect the way distances were constructed from the graph itself rather than genuine external spatial structure.
